transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… what brings me in is that I’m scared of how I eat sometimes. Like once I start, especially if I’m alone in the kitchen, it’s like I’m not fully in charge anymore. I’ll be standing there telling myself, Janet, put it away, just stop, and then I don’t. I keep going.

And it sounds silly saying “the kitchen,” because everybody eats in the kitchen, right? Mine’s always been sort of the gathering place, even when my daughter was younger and doing homework at the table… but now when I’m by myself in there, it can turn into this thing where I feel like I’ve stepped aside and I can’t make myself stop. That’s the part that scared me enough to come in.
Do you usually feel guilty or ashamed after one of these eating episodes?

Yes… yeah, I do. Pretty much right after. I’ll sit there looking at what’s left, or the wrappers, or whatever, and I just feel awful about myself.

It’s not even only the food, though that bothers me too, like if it was something I bought thinking my daughter might want some when she came by, or something I was going to make last a few days. Then I think, Janet, you’re too old to be acting like this, what is wrong with you. And I get really ashamed, just sitting there making promises to myself that I’m not going to do it again.
Do you feel like you're unable to control what or how much you're eating during these episodes?

Yes… that’s exactly it. It’s not like I just decide, oh, I’m going to have too much. It feels more like once I’ve started, especially if I’m alone in the kitchen, something kind of takes over.

I’ll be telling myself the whole time, Janet, put it away, stop now, you don’t need more, and then my hands are still reaching for it. And then I think about how my kitchen used to be such a normal place, you know, where people would sit and talk, and now sometimes it feels like this trap when I’m in there by myself.

So… yes. I feel like I can’t control it in those moments.
How often do these episodes of eating out of control happen?

Most weeks, I think. I actually tried to look back at my kitchen calendar—you know, the one where I write down food bank days and appointments and all that—and when I really pay attention, it’s been happening a lot longer than I wanted to admit.

Often it’s once or twice in a week. Not every single day, but… most weeks, for months now. I kind of lose track because the weeks all run together, especially around the food bank schedule, but yeah, it’s been many months.
Do you ever try to make up for these eating episodes by doing things like exercising, vomiting, or using laxatives?

Um… I don’t think so? I mean, I’ll tell myself I’m going to “be good” the next day, which is such a silly thing to say at my age, but I do say it. Like I’ll stand there by the sink thinking, okay, tomorrow I’ll eat better, I’ll get myself together.

But as far as… vomiting or laxatives, no, that’s not really something I do. Exercise… I mean, I’m not exactly out there jogging around the neighborhood. I’ll think about walking more, and then I get distracted because there’s laundry or I have to check the pantry or I remember I forgot to call someone back. So no, not in that way, I don’t think I try to make up for it like that.
Do you usually feel very hungry before these episodes where you feel like you're not in control of your eating?

Not usually, no. I mean, sometimes I’m a little snacky, I guess, but a lot of the time it’s after I’ve already had supper. My stomach isn’t really asking for anything.

I’ll be putting dishes away or checking if I need to add something to the grocery list, and then I open the pantry or the fridge, just to look, and I start picking at things. And then somehow it turns into more than picking. So it’s not really hunger, not the normal kind.
Do you feel like you're eating really fast during these episodes where you feel out of control?

Yeah… I think I do. I don’t really notice it right away, but then I catch myself eating so fast I’m barely even tasting it. Like if I made a casserole, or muffins—those banana ones I make when the bananas get too spotty, because I hate wasting them—I’ll just be standing there at the counter taking bite after bite.

And it’s strange because I’m acting like I’m in a rush, like somebody’s waiting on me or I have to be somewhere, but there’s nowhere I need to be. I’m just… eating fast, almost before my brain catches up.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past few months?

I’m not really sure, honestly. I don’t weigh myself much—our scale is in the bathroom closet, and half the time there’s towels piled in front of it because I reorganized that closet and then never really finished it.

My clothes maybe feel a little different some days, but then I also put things in the dryer too long, so I don’t know if that means anything. I haven’t noticed some big sudden change, I don’t think.
Do you think you're eating an excessive amount of food during these episodes where you feel out of control?

Yes… I think so. I don’t always want to call it that, because it feels embarrassing, but it’s more than a normal amount.

Like some afternoons, if I’ve been at the food bank or if I baked something for one of the senior-center things—banana bread, usually, because people like that and it’s easy to slice—I’ll come home and start with leftovers, like a full plate. And then I’ll have a couple slices of the banana bread, and then chips, maybe cheese, and then I remember there are cookies in the tin on top of the fridge.

And afterward I’ll look at what’s gone and think, “I would never serve somebody all that as one meal.” So… yeah, it’s excessive.
Do you often think very critically about yourself after these eating episodes?

Yes… I do. I get really hard on myself afterward.

I’ll sit there and think, why did I do that again? Especially if it was food I meant to share, like something I baked for somebody or was saving. Then I feel like I wasted it, or ruined it, and I start thinking I’m too old to be acting this way. Like I should have better control by now.

And then I do that thing where I promise myself, okay, that’s it, it won’t happen again. I’ll clean up the kitchen, put the containers away, maybe wipe the counter twice even though it’s already clean… but mostly I’m just sitting there feeling ashamed.
